correctness.rationale: The Henson Fraisse extension argument yields t1=I,t2=I²+D,t3=I³+3ID+3J. Every finite tree is generated from a smaller tree by attaching a leaf, and taking the minimum of recursively sorted rooted codes over all roots is an exact isomorphism invariant and complete canonical key. An independent-mask brute-force census over all such trees, with counts 1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23,47,106, finds precisely one repeated (I,D) at n10 and none earlier, with (160,8649). The two explicit nonisomorphic trees yield J=578337,578961. Six separate 8-state transfer-DP checks independently recover the three pattern contributions on each witness. No finite computation is extrapolated beyond n10.

originality.rationale: Closest full-text published treatments yield the finite-extension identities or much broader existence of indistinguishable trees without proving the first joint (I,D) collision threshold. The existing n7 full-graph result is credited, not reused as a new theorem; its n7 witness is not tree/tree and no tree collision through n10 follows from it. The new claim is the unique first tree-to-tree fibre at n10 and its ternary separation, not a universal counting identity. Actual published-finding corpus exact and alias searches and pertinent literature texts were inspected; further historical equivalent tables are a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical graph-theoretic numeric tables may contain the same joint I,D first collision with different nomenclature.

The published connected-partition and general independent-set theorems are mathematically adjacent, but neither yields this cutoff without an additional exhaustive comparison; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Natural order-theoretic/model-theoretic invariant t1 and t2 measures low-arity pointwise orbit information over named trees. The precise first failure and its entire first fibre are a motivated, finite complete reconstruction threshold, not an arbitrary cherry-picked graph. That the unique pair has identical degree multisets but differing t3 yields an exact hierarchy of logical discrimination. Exhaustive completeness and the exact cutoff, not merely code or novelty, support value; nothing is asserted for larger trees.
